spans.section: 1.7 Privacy Impact Analysis: Given the amount and type of data collected, discuss the privacy risks identified and how they were mitigated.
spans.explanation: States the overall assessed level of privacy risk.

spans.text: The minimum amount of personally identifiable information is collected to satisfy the purpose of this system.
spans.section: 1.7 Privacy Impact Analysis: Given the amount and type of data collected, discuss the privacy risks identified and how they were mitigated.
spans.explanation: Data minimization is presented in the privacy-risk analysis as limiting the PII collected to what the system requires.

spans.text: The risks are mitigated using various control mechanisms. See below: All users must be uniquely identified and authenticated prior to accessing the application. Access to data is restricted.
spans.section: 1.7 Privacy Impact Analysis: Given the amount and type of data collected, discuss the privacy risks identified and how they were mitigated.
spans.explanation: Explicitly states that risks are mitigated through controls and identifies authentication and restricted access as those controls.

spans.text: During this period, the stored information may be at risk for viewing by unauthorized parties, data loss or destruction and non-availability.
spans.section: 3.3 Privacy Impact Analysis: Please discuss the risks associated with the length of time data is retained and how those risks are mitigated.
spans.explanation: Identifies unauthorized viewing, data loss or destruction, and non-availability as risks during retention.

spans.text: Access to computerized files are protected by access control software, physical access controls and if warranted, password-protected.
spans.section: 3.3 Privacy Impact Analysis: Please discuss the risks associated with the length of time data is retained and how those risks are mitigated.
spans.explanation: Presents software, physical, and password access protections in direct response to the stated retention risks.

spans.text: SORN USDA/FSA-2 States: Program documents are destroyed within 6 years after end of participation.
spans.section: 3.3 Privacy Impact Analysis: Please discuss the risks associated with the length of time data is retained and how those risks are mitigated.
spans.explanation: Provides a defined destruction period that limits how long program records remain exposed to retention-related risks.

spans.text: According to Records Management DR3080-001 Disposition of Inactive Records: Records and other documents that are no longer sufficiently active to warrant retention in office space shall be removed as rapidly as possible by: (a) transfer to a Federal Records Center, or (b) transfer to a records retention facility meeting the requirements of 36 CFR Chapter 12, Subchapter B Records Management, Subpart K, 1228.224 through 1228.244, or (c) if authorized, by disposal. (See Appendix B - Records Disposition Procedures.)
spans.section: 3.3 Privacy Impact Analysis: Please discuss the risks associated with the length of time data is retained and how those risks are mitigated.
spans.explanation: Describes disposition procedures for transferring or disposing of inactive records as part of the response to retention risks.

spans.section: 6.5 Privacy Impact Analysis: Describe how notice is provided to individuals, and how the risks associated with individuals being unaware of the collection are mitigated.
spans.explanation: States that the risk of individuals being unaware of collection is assessed as moderate.

spans.text: Notification is automatically provided in the system of records notice (Federal Register publication): SORN: USDA/FSA-2 - Farm Records File (Automated) and USDA/FSA-14 - Applicant/Borrower.
spans.section: 6.5 Privacy Impact Analysis: Describe how notice is provided to individuals, and how the risks associated with individuals being unaware of the collection are mitigated.
spans.explanation: Identifies publication of system-of-records notices as the notification mechanism addressing the notice risk.

spans.text: The risk associated with redress is considered low, as the public does not have access to the system or the data.
spans.section: 7.5 Privacy Impact Analysis: Please discuss the privacy risks associated with the redress available to individuals and how those risks are mitigated.
spans.explanation: Assesses the privacy risk associated with available redress as low.

spans.text: While the public cannot access the system to update or change their personal information, they may update their information using form AD 2530 and submit to the appropriate FSA official. The FSA official will in turn update the system based on the information provided.
spans.section: 7.5 Privacy Impact Analysis: Please discuss the privacy risks associated with the redress available to individuals and how those risks are mitigated.
spans.explanation: Explains the alternative process through which individuals can submit corrections and have an FSA official update the system.

spans.text: The main risk associated with privacy is the exposure to unauthorized access to privacy information. This risk is considered moderate.
spans.section: 8.6 Privacy Impact Analysis: Given the sensitivity and scope of the information collected, as well as any information sharing conducted on the system, what privacy risks were identified and how do the security controls mitigate them?
spans.explanation: Identifies unauthorized access to privacy information as the main privacy risk and assesses it as moderate.

spans.text: Mitigating controls are in place to ensure privacy risks are minimal. Mitigated controls are mapped back to SSP in CSAM. Quarterly access reviews are done to ensure controls are mitigated.
spans.section: 8.6 Privacy Impact Analysis: Given the sensitivity and scope of the information collected, as well as any information sharing conducted on the system, what privacy risks were identified and how do the security controls mitigate them?
spans.explanation: Explicitly presents mapped mitigating controls and quarterly access reviews as measures for minimizing the unauthorized-access risk.

spans.section: 9.2 Does the project employ technology which may raise privacy concerns? If so please discuss their implementation.
spans.explanation: Answers that the project does not employ technology that may raise privacy concerns.
